summary.description: Groups the reviewed graph into circles that organize the story’s scroll. It uses the same deterministic community rule as the client, so narration stays attached to the circle shown on screen. It orders circles by the main people’s birth years and retains their internal ties.
summary.input: the reviewed graph
summary.output: ordered story circles and their internal ties

summary.description: Identifies the metaphors that carry the story’s argument and settles their target-language wording before translation begins. It keeps a source image only when the target language uses it; otherwise it replaces the image with its plain meaning, so repeated passages share one usable choice.
summary.input: the meta story
summary.output: a recurring-image glossary

summary.description: Selects the people who anchor the theme and maps their work into subtopics and eras. It also proposes missing people who would fill gaps. Event locations and titles supplement short registry profiles, which gives place-based themes evidence beyond occupations.
summary.input: the person registry
summary.output: a themed story plan and person selection

summary.description: Collects all dated life events for the selected people and orders them by year. It leaves relevance and chapter placement to later steps, because early chapter ranges come from incomplete summaries and can exclude events that matter.
summary.input: the selected people and life events
summary.output: a chronological list of dated events

summary.description: Judges the event pool against the story’s theme and keeps only landmark contributions with a direct, lasting effect. It records why each event belongs or fails, so later chapters rest on claims instead of chronology. The step rejects uncertain cases to prevent biographical background from shaping the story.
summary.input: the unfiltered event pool
summary.output: essential events with relevance reasons

summary.description: Places each chapter in the wider events that directly changed the featured people’s lives or work. It leaves empty space when no event clears that test, keeping the background tied to the biography instead of filling the period with famous history.
summary.input: the chapters and selected people
summary.output: chapters with relevant historical context

summary.description: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into a single graph. It keeps direct ties with each person’s account of the relationship, and retains acquaintances only when they connect multiple selected people—the bridges that reveal overlap across their worlds.
summary.input: the selected people and ego networks
summary.output: a social graph with shared acquaintances

summary.description: Reviews the merged social graph against the article evidence before clustering. It adds missing direct ties and removes or corrects weak ones, with stricter review when the main network is already dense.
summary.input: the merged social graph and article evidence
summary.output: a reviewed social graph

summary.description: Turns each detected social circle into a short factual card story. It grounds the prose in recorded ties and keeps every circle in the network’s derived order. The cards preserve a readable account of the relationships when later composition is skipped.
summary.input: the detected circles and their ties
summary.output: a card story for each circle

summary.description: Groups rated events into nearby map stops and drops events with no story value. Complete-linkage clustering keeps every event in a stop within the map distance, while rating-weighted scores choose the stops that carry the story. It orders the selected stops by time for the map journey.
summary.input: located events and per-event weights
summary.output: chronological candidate map stops

summary.description: Rates each located event by how much its place carries the story’s theme. The map branch uses these scores as clustering weights, so landmark locations shape the route while incidental settings recede.
summary.input: the chapters and life events
summary.output: geographic weights for located events

summary.description: Turns geographic clusters into short map-stop stories. It keeps places that carry the story’s turning points and drops incidental or weaker clusters, so the map follows an arc instead of becoming a gazetteer.
summary.input: the qualifying geographic clusters
summary.output: curated map stops and narrations

summary.description: Rewrites the assembled material as one story, from the header through the timeline, network, map, and conclusion. It sets the reading order and curates component text and map stops after seeing the whole, so the story follows a single argument instead of preserving earlier drafts.
summary.input: the circle narration, map stops, and background material
summary.output: a unified story and curated map stops

summary.description: Derives a dark visual system from the story’s theme and period. It leaves the article with colors, type, background geometry, and matching punctuation marks; the shared geometric motif keeps the long read and its interactive sections visually tied together.
summary.input: the story’s framing and opening
summary.output: a visual identity for the story

summary.description: Translates the meta story for the target language and preserves its structure for the interface. It reuses settled image wording and localized person names, so event titles and prose match the people stories. Local language evidence guides names for people, places, and institutions.
summary.input: the meta story and localized person data
summary.output: a localized meta story

summary.description: Writes a deeper report for each event the story offers for expansion, using the reviewed article, event material, and story context. It also revisits each event’s citations and image searches, keeping only source URLs already present in the supplied material so the depth layer can show event-specific provenance.
summary.input: reviewed events, sources, and story context
summary.output: background reports, sources, and image searches

summary.description: Draws one abstract emblem for each chapter from its visual concept. It uses the portrait treatment as a style reference, so chapter slides share the story’s light and color while their imagery remains specific to each chapter.
summary.input: draft chapter concepts and interface style
summary.output: chapter illustrations linked to life events

summary.description: Frames each chapter with an abstract image concept drawn from its events and theme. It reads the full life at once so the chapter metaphors remain distinct, then leaves only concepts tied to known chapters.
summary.input: the life chapters and their events
summary.output: an abstract concept per chapter

summary.description: Adds a German biographical source for figures identified from the Wikipedia article. Keeps reusable metadata and withholds biographical text when its license bars derivatives.
summary.input: the Wikipedia article and life dates
summary.output: Deutsche Biographie material

summary.description: Builds the narrative spine from the article set and biography material. It compares events across the whole life, assigns their importance, and groups contiguous periods into chapters. This full-life view also supports a conclusion about the work that endures.
summary.input: the article set and biography material
summary.output: a chaptered, weighted life timeline and conclusion

summary.description: Researches each proposed event against the subject’s article and event-specific related material. It expands the event into grounded prose, places, people, evidence, annotations, an icon, and image searches. It keeps an unresolved event in the story when research fails.
summary.input: event skeletons and biographical material
summary.output: researched events with sources and illustration searches

summary.description: Resolves each event’s place name to map coordinates. It prefers the researcher's modern name, so renamed historic places can appear at their current location.
summary.input: historic and modern place names
summary.output: map coordinates for resolved places

summary.description: Decides the target-language form of each person name before the biography is translated. It uses source evidence when available and preserves titles, epithets, and regnal numbers, so every document can reuse the same names.
summary.input: name evidence and person records
summary.output: a shared glossary of localized names

summary.description: Judges Commons search results against each background report and keeps only images that plainly show a named thing. It rejects name matches and stand-ins, and code limits the result to one image per search so repeated views do not crowd out other subjects.
summary.input: the report, searches, and life events
summary.output: background images for life events

summary.description: Searches both image archives for the planned searches and the event-specific searches. It keeps one record per picture; event-specific Commons results run first so shared pictures retain their event link and Commons record.
summary.input: the planned and event-specific searches
summary.output: a deduplicated pool of tagged image candidates

summary.description: Matches candidate images to life events and selects one reference portrait. It leaves events blank when metadata cannot support a direct link, which blocks memorials, generic city buildings, and other stand-ins from carrying the story.
summary.input: the ranked image candidates and life events
summary.output: event images, captions, and a reference portrait

summary.description: Plans Commons searches across the life, separating portrait candidates from event-specific subjects. It favors named things over places or later memorials, because simple keyword matching otherwise pulls commemorations into the story.
summary.input: the event skeletons
summary.output: portrait and event image searches

summary.description: Checks the chosen portrait against the person in the story, catching images whose captions mention the subject but show someone else. It rejects mismatches; a failed check leaves the portrait in place so an outage cannot remove a usable image.
summary.input: the portrait pick
summary.output: a verified or retained portrait pick

summary.description: Collects the target-language article and linked names that give later translation calls published names to follow. For unresolved comma-qualified places, it also looks up the leading place name while keeping the qualifier available for translation; the full name takes priority when it has a page.
summary.input: reviewed names, life events, and ego network
summary.output: target-language article evidence and name links

summary.description: Maps the subject’s documented relationships from the article, related material, and life events into a network that gives the later story its social setting. It limits ties to named people with direct contact so the graph shows relationships the evidence can support.
summary.input: the life events and Wikipedia material
summary.output: a documented network of personal ties

summary.description: Transforms each licensed reference portrait into the collection’s shared light-drawing style. It preserves the person’s likeness and period appearance while applying the story colors, then records the portrait for the person and their life events.
summary.input: the licensed reference portrait and interface style
summary.output: a styled portrait for the person and events

summary.description: Adds the person to the landing-page index with the dates, roles, and summary from the life events. It preserves the first appearance date while carrying the selected portrait forward for the later portrait step.
summary.input: the written life events
summary.output: the person registry

summary.description: Reviews the life story and relationship network as one reader-facing account against the available source material. It proposes corrections and prose changes across both, while the pipeline applies only high-confidence changes automatically.
summary.input: the life events, network, and Wikipedia material
summary.output: reviewed changes to events and relationships

summary.description: Builds a dark visual identity from the person’s summary and early events. It retries a palette that fails the contrast check, so the story’s historical cues remain readable.
summary.input: the person summary and early events
summary.output: a dark interface style

summary.description: Extracts prose from the person data, reports, events, and network, then translates it with the name mapping and local naming evidence. It overlays the translated fields on the English data, which preserves dates, coordinates, links, identifiers, and annotation keys.
summary.input: the English person data and name mapping
summary.output: localized person data

summary.description: Fetches the main article, candidate related articles, and image metadata for the subject. It caches this shared source material so later steps and reruns work from the same retrieved record.
summary.input: the subject or article URL
summary.output: cached Wikipedia material

summary.description: Ranks linked articles for their value in a person's life story. It keeps people, events, and personal works that can supply biographical detail, while excluding general background topics that would spend context without advancing the narrative.
summary.input: the article and outgoing link candidates
summary.output: ranked articles for biographical context
